workflow.selector_prompt: Classify the issue by its SHAPE before selecting a template, then select exactly one: if the issue mandates zero behaviour change (refactor, consolidation, extraction, dedup, moving state, renames — acceptance criteria are structural/parity-only), select 'refactor'; if the issue adds or alters observable behaviour, select 'feature'; if it mixes both, STOP and report that the issue must be split — do not proceed on a mixed issue. Record which discriminator drove your classification.

templates.label: Feature
templates.description: New capability with local hook verification, BDD/TDD, code review, then hand off the PR for human review (no auto-merge).
templates.when_to_use: Use for behaviour-adding or behaviour-changing Quecto work: the issue's acceptance criteria describe new or altered observable behaviour. Do NOT use for zero-behaviour-change restructures — use 'refactor' for those.

steps.label: Install/check local quality hooks
steps.guidance: Run `scripts/install-hooks.sh`, then verify pre-commit, pre-push, and the git --no-verify wrapper are installed/active before editing code. Hook summary: `git commit` pre-commit does NOT run unit/BDD tests; it runs quality/BDD-quality gates, `cargo fmt --check`, strict clippy, and fast guard tests. `git push` pre-push runs the full new+old suite and can take minutes. Never bypass hooks with --no-verify. Done when all three hooks are installed and active.

steps.label: Update Scenarios / Add new features
steps.guidance: First read the issue and comments with `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,comments`. Update BDD feature files and task-facing scenarios first, and identify explicit, checkable acceptance criteria for the change. BDD selection is by tag + sharding (no scenario-name filter unless implemented). The acceptance criteria identified here are the SAME checklist the later `conformance` step verifies against branch code, so make them concrete and testable. Write feature files to behaviourally-led BDD best practice: keep scenarios DECLARATIVE and behaviour-focused (describe the observable outcome from the user/stakeholder view, never implementation detail, UI selectors or incidental wiring); follow strict Given-When-Then discipline (Given = context/preconditions, When = the single triggering action, Then = the observable outcome) with one behaviour per scenario and one logical When; use ubiquitous/domain language so scenarios read as intent; do not smuggle multiple actions or assertions into conjunctive `And` steps; write reusable, well-abstracted, consistently-phrased steps; use Background only for genuinely shared context and Scenario Outline only for true data variations; scenario titles state the behaviour/intent (not "test X works"); and ensure every acceptance criterion maps to a scenario. Done when the scenarios are updated and the acceptance criteria are written down.

steps.label: Write/update unit tests (run a quick smoke check; full suite runs on push)
steps.guidance: Write or update unit tests for the change. Use these crate names: kernel `cargo test -p quecto --lib <name_substring>`; TUI `cargo test -p quecto-tui --lib <name_substring>`; never `-p quecto-agentic-harness`. Plain lib tests need no `--features`; render-harness-driven TUI BDD uses the integration `bdd` target with `--features test-harness`. Run a quick targeted smoke check to confirm tests compile; the full suite and coverage run on push. Write step tests and unit tests to the same discipline: assertions are BEHAVIOURAL (verify observable outcomes/contracts, not internal or private state), well-named, focused, DETERMINISTIC and ISOLATED (no cross-scenario state leakage or ambient/global mutation), and never HOLLOW/always-pass — each test must be able to fail, and must fail before the implementation exists (RED). Done when the new/modified tests compile and target the new behaviour.

steps.label: Ensure new/modified tests FAIL (RED) — quick targeted run only, not full suite
steps.guidance: Run a quick targeted check: only the new/modified targeted test to confirm it fails before implementation: `cargo test -p quecto --lib <name_substring>` or `cargo test -p quecto-tui --lib <name_substring>`. Do not run the whole suite here. RED evidence is required per new Then step and per new test assertion, not per test target: every new assertion must individually be shown to fail before implementation — a tautology cannot produce that evidence, so it is rejected by construction. Done when the new tests fail for the expected reason. If it fails to fail — i.e. a new test passes before implementation — it is not exercising the new behaviour, so fix the test.

steps.label: Despatch three BDD review finders (Gherkin discipline, Falsifiability, Coverage)
steps.guidance: Dispatch three narrow BDD review finders in parallel, each bound to its OWN dedicated review workflow via `workflow_spec`/`template` (never this feature workflow), launched read-only: pass `read_only: true` to `spawn` (equivalent to `disable_tools: ["write", "edit"]`) so it cannot write or edit repo files while it retains `bash`, `read`, `grep`, `find` and `agent_cmd` to inspect the changes (defense-in-depth, not a hard sandbox, since bash remains). Spawned reviewers are auto-awaited (you get a one-line completion note at your next idle turn, so an explicit `agent_cmd` `command: 'await'` is optional); read findings with `get_messages`. Give each finder the issue details, the changed BDD feature files, step tests and unit tests, and ONE angle: (1) Gherkin discipline — STRICT and uncompromising on BDD best practice: because BDD quality is foundational it must flag EVERY genuine best-practice deviation, not just egregious ones (while staying skeptical: report only real issues, never invalid or hallucinated findings), explicitly checking the checklist: DECLARATIVE/behavioural phrasing with no implementation detail in steps, strict Given-When-Then discipline, one behaviour per scenario, ubiquitous/domain language, reusable well-abstracted steps. (2) Falsifiability — for each assertion, name the implementation change that would make it fail; flag self-asserted (test-constructed) state, constant comparisons and type-level facts. (3) Coverage — full acceptance-criterion-to-scenario mapping plus boundary pinning: both sides of every numeric/size limit must be tested. There is no verify wave — the scope is small. Each finding must quote the offending line and give a concrete fix, plus file:line and severity. Finders must NOT modify code. Then address EVERY valid concern regardless of severity, not just high-priority ones: fix it, or explicitly DECLINE it with a documented rationale (reviewers can be wrong). All valid BDD concerns must be resolved before the GREEN step. Done when all three finders have returned and every valid concern is fixed or declined with rationale.

steps.label: Implement code (GREEN)
steps.guidance: Write the code needed to satisfy the failing tests. Do NOT worry about the size of a change — implement it in full. Done when the previously-failing tests pass.

steps.label: Refactor
steps.guidance: Tidy only what this change touches — naming, duplication, clarity. Keep it minimal; no speculative abstraction or unrelated cleanup.

steps.label: Ensure tests still pass
steps.guidance: Run `cargo fmt` and targeted strict clippy locally first (for kernel: `cargo clippy -p quecto --all-targets -- -D warnings`), then re-run only the targeted tests and confirm GREEN. Do not manually re-run the whole suite before commit; push/pre-push is the full-suite mechanism. Respect the 750-line file cap and strict clippy before pushing. Done when targeted tests pass and fmt/clippy are clean. If it fails, fix the code — never silence clippy — before pushing.

steps.label: Bump semver for every changed crate and sync version docs
steps.guidance: Bump the semver of every crate whose source changed in this PR before committing, so the bump goes through the same gate as the code. Determine which crates you actually modified (e.g. `git diff --name-only master...HEAD` plus unstaged changes) and bump the PATCH version in each such crate's Cargo.toml (MINOR for a notable feature). Do NOT bump crates you did not change. Keep version docs in lockstep: for the `quecto` kernel, update the README.md 'Current version: **x.y.z**' line and the matching assertion in `quecto-agentic-harness/tests/features/repo_docs.feature` so both equal the new version; for `quecto-tui`, update its Cargo.toml and any TUI version assertion; for any other crate, update whatever doc or test pins its version. Done when every changed crate's Cargo.toml and its version docs show the new, matching version and no unchanged crate was bumped.

steps.label: Commit
steps.guidance: If on the default branch, create a feature branch first. Stage only the files you changed (`git add <paths>`); never `git add -A` or `git add .` — that sweeps untracked tooling (e.g. `.claude/`) and build artifacts (e.g. `target*/`) into the commit. Remember `git commit` runs the pre-commit structure/lint/fast-guard gate, not unit/BDD feature tests. Write a clear, descriptive commit message and include any commit trailers your harness requires. Done when only the intended files are staged and committed on a feature branch.

steps.label: Push (pre-push hook will run tests and linting)
steps.guidance: Push triggers the full local gate (or validate without pushing via `scripts/pre-push.sh`): fmt, strict clippy, unit/integration/architecture/contracts/repo_docs/workflow_config, the 24-shard non-real BDD suite, region coverage at or above 87% for quecto and quecto-tui, machete and deny. The zero-cost mocked `@mock-llm` e2e lane runs by default; the live LLM suite (tagged `@manual-real-llm`) is opt-in via `QUECTO_RUN_REAL_LLM=1`. The `find.feature` "Nested .gitignore … in git repo" scenario is load-flaky under the parallel shard wave — re-run the shard before treating it as a real failure (it passes in isolation). Push may take minutes and is not hung. Fix every failure; never use --no-verify. Done when the full gate is green. If it fails only on the flaky find.feature scenario, re-run the shard; otherwise fix the failure.

steps.label: Create PR
steps.guidance: Open the PR against the default branch with gh, with a clear title and a body that summarizes the change. The required CI checks are "Unit Tests" and "Mock LLM E2E Tests". Do not claim to co-author it. Done when the PR is open and the required checks are running.

steps.label: Despatch narrow parallel review finders, verify adversarially, post one review
steps.guidance: Precondition: reviewers MUST NOT be dispatched before a PR exists; if no PR number is available, stop and complete the Create PR step first. Use `gh pr view <PR> --json id,headRefOid,state,mergeStateStatus` and `gh pr diff <PR>`. The review runs as three waves. Wave 1 — narrow parallel finders: dispatch ALL default finder angles in a SINGLE parallel batch, each spawned read-only (`read_only: true`, i.e. `disable_tools: ["write", "edit"]`, so a finder cannot write or edit repo files but retains `bash`, `read`, `grep`, `find` and `agent_cmd` to fetch the diff and inspect the code; defense-in-depth, not a hard sandbox) and bound to its OWN `review-pr` workflow, given only the PR number, head commit SHA and ONE mechanical angle. Explicitly forbid passing a raw diff: finders must fetch the diff themselves from the PR number. Finders make no GitHub writes — they never post to GitHub; they only return structured findings. Default angles: line-by-line hunk scan seeded with diff-specific failure classes; Removed-behavior audit (for every deleted/replaced line, name the invariant it enforced and where the new code re-establishes it); Cross-file tracer (callers/callees/consumers of every changed symbol); Security (injection, path traversal, secret leakage, permission gaps introduced by the diff); Performance/efficiency; Reuse + altitude (does new code re-implement an existing helper; same-defect-class grep — does the defect being fixed exist elsewhere in the codebase; bandaid vs. mechanism); Test falsifiability (for each new/changed test, name the implementation change that would make it fail; reject assertions on test-constructed state, constants, or type-guaranteed facts, and anything that would pass with the implementation reverted). Conformance to the issue acceptance criteria is NOT a finder angle — it needs whole-issue context and lives in the standalone conformance step. Each finding is structured as file:line, a one-line summary, and a concrete failure scenario (required — a finding without one is dropped). Wave 2 — adversarial verification: dedupe Wave 1 findings, then dispatch one read-only verifier per finding, in parallel, prompted to REFUTE it; each verdict is CONFIRMED, PLAUSIBLE or REFUTED and must quote the proving/disproving line. If Wave 1 returns no findings, skip Wave 2. Wave 3 — single post: the master posts exactly one submitted review via GitHub GraphQL (`addPullRequestReview` event COMMENT with comments array) carrying every surviving (non-REFUTED) finding as an INLINE review comment on the PR; if a line anchor is rejected, fall back to a review comment that still cites file:line. When multiple finders converge on the same line, treat that as a severity signal — note it on the finding. CRITICAL: SUBMIT the review, never leave it PENDING; verify submittedAt != null. Done when every surviving finding is posted inline in one submitted (non-PENDING) review on the PR.

steps.label: Fix all valid review concerns
steps.guidance: Triage each inline finding — confirm it is genuinely valid before changing anything (reviewers can be wrong). Address EVERY valid concern regardless of severity — not just the high-priority ones: fix it in the same branch, or explicitly DECLINE it with a documented rationale. Track which findings you accept versus decline; you reply to all of them in the resolve step. Done when every valid finding regardless of severity has a fix in the branch or a documented decline.

steps.label: Push changes to remote
steps.guidance: Push the fixes; the full pre-push gate runs again. Wait for it to pass before resolving threads.

steps.label: Reply to the reviewers comments on the PR and mark resolved (use graphql)
steps.guidance: Reply to EVERY review comment on the PR — for accepted findings note the fix and commit, for declined ones explain why — then resolve each thread with the GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation. Thread ids come from the PR reviewThreads connection. Done when every review thread is resolved.

steps.label: Verify the PR meets every issue acceptance criterion
steps.guidance: Read the original issue and comments with `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,comments`, then systematically verify EACH acceptance criterion from the issue (the same checklist captured in `scenarios`) against the ACTUAL branch code, citing file:line evidence, including any documentation and protocol updates the criteria require. A criterion counts as met only when the evidence is in the code — never on the PR description claims; be skeptical. Output a per-criterion table marking each met/partial/unmet with evidence, then a final verdict line: `CONFORMANCE: PASS` only if every criterion is fully met, otherwise `CONFORMANCE: FAIL` listing gaps. On `CONFORMANCE: FAIL`, fix the gaps and re-verify before reporting — do NOT merge on a FAIL. Done when the verdict is `CONFORMANCE: PASS` with file:line evidence for every criterion.

steps.label: Confirm the pre-push gate passed and report the PR (do NOT merge)
steps.guidance: Confirm the latest push's pre-push gate passed in full (coverage threshold, machete, deny, and the mocked `@mock-llm` e2e lane that runs by default; the live LLM suite is opt-in via `QUECTO_RUN_REAL_LLM=1`) and the required CI checks "Unit Tests" and "Mock LLM E2E Tests" are green. Also confirm the reviewers actually POSTED inline findings on the PR (not just a returned summary) and that all review threads are resolved. The `find.feature` "Nested .gitignore … in git repo" scenario is load-flaky — re-run the shard before treating it as a real failure. Do NOT run gh pr merge or git merge, and do NOT set auto-merge: this workflow never merges. Report the PR number and a short summary, then STOP — the master agent and a human own merging. For the PR to be mergeable the required "Unit Tests" and "Mock LLM E2E Tests" checks must be green and the verdict must be CONFORMANCE: PASS; if any review, fix, or conformance step ERRORED or did not actually run, or the push bypassed the local gate with --no-verify, report that too. Done when the gate and required checks are green, inline findings were posted, all threads are resolved, and the PR is reported as ready for review (NOT merged).

steps.label: Clean up sub agents
steps.guidance: Reviewers that have already reported completion (you received their one-line completion notes) have exited and need no cleanup. Check `get_subagents` for any sub agent still running, and only then terminate the stragglers (use agent_cmd to abort, or kill each) so no orphaned sub agents remain.

guards.message: Complete hook setup and RED/GREEN work before committing.

This workflow does NOT merge — report the PR for review and stop. Before reporting, complete code review, pass the conformance gate (CONFORMANCE: PASS), and verify the pre-push gate genuinely passed (not bypassed with --no-verify). Never run gh pr merge / git merge or set auto-merge; report the PR as ready for review instead.

templates.label: Refactor
templates.description: Behaviour-preserving restructure: gate readiness, characterize current behaviour GREEN-first, prove falsifiability by mutation, freeze the suite, refactor under it, prove parity, then review and hand off the PR for human review (no auto-merge).
templates.when_to_use: Use when the issue mandates zero behaviour change: consolidation, extraction, dedup, renames, moving state. Acceptance criteria are structural/parity-only. If the issue adds or alters observable behaviour, use 'feature'. If mixed, stop and report that the issue must be split.

steps.label: Install/check local quality hooks
steps.guidance: Run `scripts/install-hooks.sh`, then verify pre-commit, pre-push, and the git --no-verify wrapper are installed/active before editing code. Hook summary: `git commit` pre-commit does NOT run unit/BDD tests; it runs quality/BDD-quality gates, `cargo fmt --check`, strict clippy, and fast guard tests. `git push` pre-push runs the full new+old suite and can take minutes. Never bypass hooks with --no-verify. Done when all three hooks are installed and active.

steps.label: Read the issue; run the readiness gate; write the parity contract
steps.guidance: First read the issue and comments with `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,comments`. Run the READINESS GATE before any other work. BLOCKING (stop and report with a structured list of exactly what is missing, with examples of what good looks like): the issue does not explicitly mandate zero behaviour change; the touched observable surfaces cannot be enumerated; no test/render harness exists to pin a surface's behaviour; the issue mixes behavioural change with refactoring (report that it must be split). WARNING (proceed only after stating the named consequence in your notes and later in the PR body): performance characteristics of replaced specialized code not recorded — consequence: allocation/complexity regressions will be undetectable. Then write the PARITY CONTRACT: (a) the exhaustive list of observable surfaces the refactor touches; (b) per surface, the behaviours that must be provably identical afterwards, in behaviour language first, including boundary cases — exact-fit vs overflow widths, empty/one/many items, both sides of every numeric limit, scroll-window edges, full-set vs visible-window computations; (c) performance characteristics of specialized code being replaced (allocation patterns, single-pass vs recompute, cached values) that the shared replacement must not regress. Never infer facts not verified against the actual code — verify what the current code ACTUALLY does at each boundary before recording it; mark anything you cannot determine as __UNRESOLVED__ rather than guessing, and resolve or escalate every marker before the characterize step. Structural goals from the issue (e.g. 'one shared renderer', 'net LOC decrease') are recorded as REVIEW-TIME checks for the conformance step — they must NEVER become test assertions. The contract starts as draft and must be marked approved (all __UNRESOLVED__ markers cleared, gate passed) before characterization begins. Done when the gate has passed (or warnings are explicitly accepted with consequences stated) and the parity contract is approved with a per-surface behaviour checklist.

steps.label: Write characterization tests that pass GREEN on the unmodified code
steps.guidance: BEFORE touching production code, write tests that pin the current behaviour of every surface in the parity contract, using the real harness and real inputs: construct the widget/component, drive actual keystrokes and navigation, assert on rendered frames and observable outcomes. Use these crate names: kernel `cargo test -p quecto --lib <name_substring>`; TUI `cargo test -p quecto-tui --lib <name_substring>`; render-harness-driven TUI BDD uses the integration `bdd` target with `--features test-harness`. HARD BAN: no test may read production source files and assert on their text (contains/regex on helper names, field names, struct layout) — such a test verifies the diff, not the behaviour, and is rejected on sight; equally banned are assertions on test-constructed state, constants, or type-guaranteed facts. Where a scenario title or step name claims an action ('the user filters', 'moves selection'), the step body MUST perform that action — a When that sends no input is a defect. Choose the cheapest runtime class that is still truthful about the behaviour: a TUI widget's behaviour is observable only through the render harness, never below it. Cover the boundary cases from the parity contract explicitly. Run the tests against the UNMODIFIED code: all must pass GREEN. A characterization test that fails on master means you misunderstood current behaviour — investigate before proceeding. Done when the full characterization set is GREEN on untouched code and maps to every row of the parity contract.

steps.label: Prove each characterization test can fail (mutation evidence)
steps.guidance: This replaces the feature flow's RED gate: characterization tests pass before the change by design, so falsifiability is proven by MUTATION instead. For each characterization assertion (per assertion, not per test target), temporarily introduce a plausible defect of the class the refactor could cause — an off-by-one in width arithmetic, computing over the visible window instead of the full set, dropping a clamp, ignoring an input key — confirm the test FAILS for that reason, then revert the mutation cleanly (git checkout/stash; verify a clean working tree afterwards). A test that survives every relevant mutation is hollow: fix or delete it. Record a mutation log (test -> mutation -> observed failure) as evidence for the PR body. Done when every characterization assertion has demonstrated it can fail and the working tree is clean and GREEN again.

steps.label: Despatch characterization review finders, then FREEZE the suite
steps.guidance: Dispatch three narrow review finders in parallel BEFORE the refactor begins, each bound to its OWN dedicated review workflow via `workflow_spec`/`template` (never this refactor workflow), launched read-only: pass `read_only: true` to `spawn` so a finder cannot write or edit repo files while retaining `bash`, `read`, `grep`, `find` and `agent_cmd` to inspect the changes. Give each finder the parity contract, the mutation log, and the new characterization tests, with ONE angle: (1) Falsifiability — for each assertion, name the implementation change that would make it fail; flag any source-text assertion, self-asserted state, constant comparison, or step body that does not perform the action its title claims. (2) Coverage — full parity-contract-to-test mapping: every surface and boundary in the contract has a pinning test, both sides of every numeric limit. (3) Gherkin discipline for any BDD scenarios, per repo BDD best practice. Address EVERY valid concern: fix it, or explicitly DECLINE it with documented rationale. Then FREEZE the suite: record the characterization test files and their content hashes (e.g. `git hash-object`) as the freeze manifest. From this point until the parity step these tests are READ-ONLY; any necessary edit must be recorded with written rationale and re-run through mutation evidence — silent edits are gate violations. Done when all finders returned, every concern is fixed or declined with rationale, and the freeze manifest is recorded.

steps.label: Perform the refactor under the frozen suite
steps.guidance: Now restructure: extract the shared helper, move the state clusters, redirect call sites. Rules: (a) the characterization tests are the oracle — after each coherent slice, re-run them; they must pass UNMODIFIED. (b) When forcing an existing abstraction to serve a new call site, EXTEND the abstraction to fit the data (add the field, add the full-set computation) rather than shoehorning the data to fit the abstraction (stringified values, per-window recomputes) — impedance mismatch at a call site is a design signal, not something to paper over. (c) Keep a DELETION LEDGER: for every line you delete, name the invariant it enforced and where the new code re-establishes it. (d) No behaviour or visual change, no speculative abstraction; respect the 750-line file cap. Done when the refactor is complete and the frozen suite is GREEN with zero test edits (or only logged, re-mutation-tested ones).

steps.label: Prove parity: behaviour, performance, and the issue's quantitative claims
steps.guidance: Run `cargo fmt` and targeted strict clippy first, then produce parity EVIDENCE, not assertion, as a table (surface x behaviour x evidence x verdict): (1) Behavioural — the frozen characterization suite and all pre-existing targeted suites for touched crates pass with ZERO modifications to pre-existing tests; diff the test tree against the freeze manifest and explain any delta. (2) Visual — where frames are pinned, before/after rendered output is identical for every surface in the contract. (3) Performance — for each piece of specialized code replaced by shared code, state what the old code avoided (allocations per keystroke, recomputation, extra passes) and show the new path does not reintroduce it, citing the mechanism. (4) Quantitative — measure any numeric criteria from the issue (e.g. net LOC decrease) and record the number. Done when all four parity classes have recorded evidence and fmt/clippy are clean. If any parity class fails, fix the production code — never the frozen tests — and re-verify.

steps.label: Bump semver for every changed crate and sync version docs
steps.guidance: Bump the semver of every crate whose source changed in this PR before committing, so the bump goes through the same gate as the code. Determine which crates you actually modified (e.g. `git diff --name-only master...HEAD` plus unstaged changes) and bump the PATCH version in each such crate's Cargo.toml. Do NOT bump crates you did not change. Keep version docs in lockstep: for the `quecto` kernel, update the README.md 'Current version: **x.y.z**' line and the matching assertion in `quecto-agentic-harness/tests/features/repo_docs.feature`; for `quecto-tui`, its Cargo.toml and any TUI version assertion; for any other crate, whatever doc or test pins its version. Done when every changed crate's Cargo.toml and its version docs show the new, matching version and no unchanged crate was bumped.

steps.label: Commit
steps.guidance: If on the default branch, create a feature branch first. Stage only the files you changed (`git add <paths>`); never `git add -A` or `git add .` — that sweeps untracked tooling and build artifacts into the commit. Write a clear, descriptive commit message that summarizes the parity evidence, and include any commit trailers your harness requires. Done when only the intended files are staged and committed on a feature branch.

steps.label: Push (pre-push hook will run tests and linting)
steps.guidance: Push triggers the full local gate (or validate without pushing via `scripts/pre-push.sh`): fmt, strict clippy, unit/integration/architecture/contracts/repo_docs/workflow_config, the 24-shard non-real BDD suite, region coverage at or above 87% for quecto and quecto-tui, machete and deny. The `find.feature` "Nested .gitignore … in git repo" scenario is load-flaky under the parallel shard wave — re-run the shard before treating it as a real failure. Push may take minutes and is not hung. Fix every failure; never use --no-verify. Done when the full gate is green.

steps.label: Create PR
steps.guidance: Open the PR against the default branch with gh. The body MUST state: the parity contract summary, the mutation-evidence summary, the freeze-manifest status (characterization tests unmodified: yes/no, with rationale for any logged edit), performance-parity notes, measured quantitative criteria (e.g. LOC delta), and any accepted readiness-gate WARNINGs with their named consequences. The required CI checks are "Unit Tests" and "Mock LLM E2E Tests". Do not claim to co-author it. Done when the PR is open and the required checks are running.

Wave 2 — adversarial verification: dedupe, then dispatch one read-only verifier per finding, in parallel, prompted to REFUTE it; verdicts are CONFIRMED, PLAUSIBLE or REFUTED and must quote the proving/disproving line. If Wave 1 returns no findings, skip Wave 2. Done when every surviving finding is posted inline in one submitted (non-PENDING) review on the PR.

steps.label: Fix all valid review concerns
steps.guidance: Triage each inline finding — confirm it is genuinely valid before changing anything (reviewers can be wrong). Address EVERY valid concern regardless of severity: fix it in the same branch, or explicitly DECLINE it with a documented rationale. Fixes to production code must keep the frozen characterization suite green; any fix that requires changing a characterization test goes back through mutation evidence with a logged rationale. Done when every valid finding has a fix in the branch or a documented decline.

steps.label: Push changes to remote
steps.guidance: Push the fixes; the full pre-push gate runs again. Wait for it to pass before resolving threads.

steps.label: Reply to the reviewers comments on the PR and mark resolved (use graphql)
steps.guidance: Reply to EVERY review comment on the PR — for accepted findings note the fix and commit, for declined ones explain why — then resolve each thread with the GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation. Thread ids come from the PR reviewThreads connection. Done when every review thread is resolved.

steps.label: Verify the PR against the issue AND the parity contract
steps.guidance: Read the original issue and comments with `gh issue view <N> --json title,body,comments`, then verify EACH acceptance criterion against the ACTUAL branch code with file:line evidence — never PR-description claims; be skeptical. Refactor-specific checks: structural goals (e.g. single shared helper, extracted state clusters) are verified HERE by code inspection — this is why they were never test assertions; behaviour unchanged per the recorded parity evidence; quantitative criteria measured (e.g. net LOC decrease); and NO test asserts on production source text — grep the test tree for reads of src files inside assertions and treat any hit as a FAIL. Output a per-criterion table marking each met/partial/unmet with evidence, then a final verdict line: `CONFORMANCE: PASS` only if every criterion is fully met, otherwise `CONFORMANCE: FAIL` listing gaps. On FAIL, fix the gaps and re-verify before reporting — do NOT merge on a FAIL. Done when the verdict is `CONFORMANCE: PASS` with file:line evidence for every criterion.

steps.label: Confirm the pre-push gate passed and report the PR (do NOT merge)
steps.guidance: Confirm the latest push's pre-push gate passed in full and the required CI checks "Unit Tests" and "Mock LLM E2E Tests" are green. Confirm the reviewers actually POSTED inline findings on the PR and all review threads are resolved. Confirm the PR body carries the parity evidence, mutation log and freeze-manifest status. The `find.feature` "Nested .gitignore … in git repo" scenario is load-flaky — re-run the shard before treating it as a real failure. Do NOT run gh pr merge or git merge, and do NOT set auto-merge: this workflow never merges. Report the PR number and a short summary, then STOP — the master agent and a human own merging. If any review, fix, or conformance step ERRORED or did not actually run, or the push bypassed the local gate with --no-verify, report that too. Done when the gate and required checks are green, inline findings were posted, all threads are resolved, and the PR is reported as ready for review (NOT merged).

steps.label: Clean up sub agents
steps.guidance: Reviewers that have already reported completion have exited and need no cleanup. Check `get_subagents` for any sub agent still running, and only then terminate the stragglers (abort or kill each) so no orphaned sub agents remain.

guards.message: Complete the readiness gate, characterization, mutation evidence, freeze, restructure and parity proof before committing.

This workflow does NOT merge — report the PR for review and stop. Before reporting, complete code review, pass the conformance gate (CONFORMANCE: PASS), verify parity evidence is recorded, and verify the pre-push gate genuinely passed (not bypassed with --no-verify). Never run gh pr merge / git merge or set auto-merge.
